text_summary.body: Jehoiakim "slept with his fathers" and Jehoiachin, eighteen, reigned three months; Egypt no longer campaigned beyond its border.

setting.body: Wiseman (via Guzik) dates Jehoiakim's death about December 598, three months before the chronicle's capture of Jerusalem (March 597).

terminology.gloss: Regnal-death formula in Kings; does not by itself state the manner of death.

competing_reconstructions.label: Natural death in Jerusalem ("slept with his fathers")
competing_reconstructions.summary: The regnal formula used for peaceful deaths.

competing_reconstructions.label: Dishonoured death / unburied
proponents: Josephus, Ant. 10.6.3 (killed by Nebuchadnezzar and thrown before the walls)
competing_reconstructions.summary: Jeremiah foretells "the burial of a donkey"; Josephus narrates his execution.

competing_reconstructions.label: Bound for Babylon
competing_reconstructions.summary: Chronicles says Nebuchadnezzar bound him in fetters to carry him to Babylon, without saying he arrived.

commentary.paraphrase: Guzik notes the divergent accounts of Jehoiakim's end and treats Chronicles' "eight years old" for Jehoiachin as a probable copyist's error (some manuscripts read eighteen).

not_applicable.constraints: Dated through the capture event (three months later).
not_applicable.locations: Jerusalem implied; no location research needed.
